universal_lens: The phenomenological transition from imagination to hallucination is modeled as a bifurcation in an autonomous dynamical system. The loss of volitional agency corresponds to the vanishing of a control parameter, driving the cognitive state toward a spontaneous symmetry-breaking limit cycle.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, pseudo-hallucinations represent high-conviction latent features emerging spontaneously from noisy telemetry without explicit agent input. Bayesian inference treats these 'inner voices' as unmodeled priors that must be conformally calibrated against objective reality metrics to prevent delusional overfitting.

The state-transition model tracks the drift from controlled simulation (imagination) to involuntary execution (hallucination), requiring strict boundary conditions at the distinctest vision limit.

The derivation begins by formalizing the phenomenological space of perception as a topological manifold \mathcal{M}. We define three distinct sub-manifolds: Imagination (\mathcal{I}), Pseudo-hallucination (\mathcal{P}), and Hallucination (\mathcal{H}). The primary operator governing transitions between these states is the Volitional Control Vector, \vec{v}. In \mathcal{I}, \vec{v} is maximal; the subject actively constructs the imagery. As we transition to \mathcal{P}, the text notes that phenomena are 'almost impossible to produce them at will,' implying \vec{v} \rightarrow 0. However, \mathcal{P} lacks the 'character of objective reality' found in \mathcal{H}. This introduces a secondary metric, the Reality Scalar, \rho. Thus, \mathcal{P} is defined by the dual constraints: \vec{v} \approx 0 and \rho < \rho_{critical}. The duality emerges in the spatial projection: \mathcal{P} projects outward only to the 'limit of distinctest vision,' acting as a localized boundary layer before full externalization into \mathcal{H}. The failure mode, or singularity, occurs when the system attempts to apply volitional operators to a state already residing in \mathcal{P}; the lack of agency causes a catastrophic collapse of the predictive model, manifesting as the 'unforeseen remarks' of the inner voices. Mathematically, this is a bifurcation point where the eigenvalues of the cognitive stability matrix cross into the right half-plane, driven entirely by endogenous noise rather than exogenous stimuli.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive lineage traces back to William James's foundational work on the stream of consciousness, specifically his categorization of ideational states. It mathematically prefigures modern predictive coding theories, where top-down priors (hallucinations) clash with bottom-up sensory evidence. Historically, it bridges 19th-century experimental psychology with contemporary dynamical systems theory applied to cognitive science, establishing the rigorous separation between agency and perception.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling the subject requires treating the mind as a multi-agent system. The 'executive self' attempts to maintain control via \vec{v}, while a latent, autonomous generator produces the 'inner voices.' When the environment grows quiet, the executive self lowers its vigilance, inadvertently granting the autonomous generator access to the phonological loop. The opposing actor here is the subconscious pattern matcher, which hijacks the perceptual apparatus under low-noise conditions.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: To prevent anti-collinearity, we must veto any mapping that equates pseudo-hallucinations purely with imagination. The leakage condition arises if the GSE interprets spontaneous internal alerts as user commands. A strict veto is required: if \vec{v} is absent, the output must be flagged as an observational anomaly rather than an actionable directive, preserving the integrity of the objective reality metric \rho.
